blocks.text: On Good and Evil, Light and Darkness, and the Highest State of Service
The teacher told his students that the world is not split into light and darkness. We are the ones who split it that way, with our own eyes.
Everything a person sees is colored by the state of his mind: goodness, passion, ignorance, or some mix of them.
Inside every person there is a light that seeks goodness, a fire that reaches for passion, and a fog that pulls toward ignorance.
These three states shape how we see things: goodness makes things clear, passion stirs things up, and ignorance clouds everything.
Every Action Is Colored by the Gunas
There is no action without a motive, and no motive that isn't colored by some state of mind.
So every action reflects the inner colors of the person doing it.
The same task — work, war, teaching, trade, art, or even kindness — can bring different results, depending on the state of mind behind it.
In ignorance, everything brings fear, attachment, destruction, or numbness.
In passion, we feel desire, tiredness, struggle, and rivalry — and these color how we see the world.
Goodness brings clarity, calm, understanding, and harmony.
Each color creates its own world. So depending on our state, the world can look evil or good, full of light or full of darkness.
But in truth, the world never changes. It is neither good nor evil — just like nature itself.
Knowledge Also Comes in Three Kinds
Knowledge is like water: it takes the shape of whatever holds it — the shape of the mind. The same words can be understood in very different ways.
And knowledge itself is colored by the three states.
Knowledge in ignorance makes a person even more blind, and he starts defending his own blindness.
Knowledge in passion makes a person proud. He starts chasing praise instead of truth.
Knowledge in goodness makes a person gentle and thoughtful — but sometimes too detached to act in the world.
The Highest Sage Has Gone Beyond the Three States
These three states are the gunas of material nature.
A wise person does not spin along with them. He stands above the gunas. He watches them move, but he himself stays still.
He stands above goodness, passion, and ignorance, untouched by matter.
Whoever reaches spiritual awareness is not colored by any guna. He has a freedom that nothing in this world can give.

Still, a master understands the other states. He doesn't argue with ignorance — he looks for a way to reach its heart. He doesn't fight passion — he guides it. He doesn't fall asleep in goodness — he uses it as a tool for clarity.

He knows the ignorant are not to blame for their harshness — they simply cannot see. The passionate are not to blame for not listening — they are burning with desire. And even the good are not perfect — they can fail to act, fail to grow, and fall at any moment.
Service Is the Highest Nature of the Soul
The heart of the soul, and the heart of love, is service.

Without service, there is no happy family, no friendship, no love. A mother serves her children, and her children serve her back with care. Friends serve each other with attention. A student serves his teacher by showing gratitude.
Without service, a country has no order, no wisdom, no harmony. A ruler must serve his people, and the people must serve their ruler.
Service is not slavery, and it's not something low. It means giving yourself to something greater than you — to your family, to people, to society, to truth, to beauty, or to God.
The whole world stands on service. Just as a body lives only as long as its heart keeps beating.
Only Pure Service Goes Beyond the Gunas
Like everything else in this world, service too can be colored by the gunas.
Service done for profit is colored by passion. Service done out of fear is colored by ignorance. Service done out of kindness is colored by goodness.
But service done out of love is colored by nothing at all.
This is not an outer action, but an inner state — serving the Source of life, the Supersoul. It means both Belonging and Trust in the Source.
Devotion to the One who drives the chariot and lives in the heart of every being.
This kind of service frees us from the three gunas, purifies the mind, and opens the way home.
The highest state is serving the Supreme with a pure heart.

Whoever serves the Supreme with love takes on the nature of the Supreme. This is how we become free from the gunas and from matter. We gain a peace that time cannot touch, and a love that never fades, flowing from the source of all that exists.
Then the soul becomes what it always was — a spark of eternal light.
